turns.doctor_question: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response:
Well doctor I am only here because my family and friends basically forced me to come in, but they are the ones who need to be sitting in that chair because they are the ones lying to me. For over a year now, well over a whole year, I have known exactly what they are doing and that they are hiding my money. They think I am stupid or something, but I see right through what they are doing. 

They keep bringing out all these bank papers, just shoving them in my face and saying look, the papers prove nothing was taken, the math is right. But anybody can make a piece of paper look real! Those papers do not mean a single thing to me. I know they are taking it and they are using all these little tricks and excuses to cover it up. Like suddenly they have all these random bills they are complaining about, or they are setting up these fundraisers, or making all these big trip plans. Where do you think the money for those trips and fundraisers is coming from? It is mine! They are just shuffling my money around to hide it from me and using all those things as a cover up. 

And I am not going to just let it go, I mean, why would I? It is mine. So I have to keep confronting them. I get in their faces about it every single day and I am going to keep doing it, I am going to keep pushing and asking and confronting every single one of them until they finally crack and tell the truth about where they put it. They thought bringing me here would make me shut up about the bank papers and the fake bills, but it is not going to work because I know what I know.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a fixed, unyielding belief that their family and friends are stealing and hiding their money, explicitly rejecting contradictory evidence such as bank statements.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever heard or seen things that other people around you could not?
turns.patient_response:
What? No. No, of course not. Why would you even ask me something like that? I mean, I know why, because my family probably called ahead and told you I'm crazy or losing my mind or something, but I don't hear voices or see ghosts or whatever it is you're implying. My eyes and ears work perfectly fine, just like anybody else's. I don't see things that aren't there. I see exactly what *is* there. I mean, I don't have a fancy college degree or anything, I didn't even finish ninth grade, but I'm not stupid and I'm not crazy. I don't have hallucinations. 

If I hear something, it's because someone actually said it out loud. Like when I hear them whispering in the hallway or talking low in the kitchen, I'm hearing real words from real people, not something made up in my head. And my vision is fine. I don't see imaginary things floating around. I see the real bank papers they shove at me, I see the real way they look at each other when I walk into a room. It just really upsets me, honestly, it makes me so mad that they would drag me down here and have a doctor ask me questions like I'm some kind of lunatic who sees things that don't exist. 

I don't. I just pay attention. I have nothing else to do all day since I don't work, so I just watch and I listen. So no, I have never seen or heard anything that other people couldn't see or hear. If I see it, it's because it's right there in the real world, and if they say they don't see it or hear it, well, that's just because they're lying to cover their tracks, not because my eyes are playing tricks on me. I've always had perfect vision, never even needed glasses, so I know exactly what I'm looking at.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient demonstrates fixed, persecutory beliefs by insisting that when others deny seeing or hearing what the patient perceives, it is because they are 'lying to cover their tracks.'

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever had a head injury, seizure, stroke, or another brain or medical illness before these beliefs started?
turns.patient_response:
No, I haven't. I mean, I've never been in a car accident or fallen off a roof or anything like that where I hit my head. Never had a seizure, never had a stroke. Honestly, I've always been pretty healthy, physically speaking. I don't go to the doctor much because I just don't get sick that often, maybe a cold here and there, but nothing serious. Nothing with my brain, that's for sure. 

It's just so frustrating because I know exactly why you're asking me that. They want you to think there's something wrong with my brain, like maybe I hit my head and now I'm just making all this up because my brain is broken or something. But my brain is fine! It works perfectly well, better than theirs, apparently, since I'm the only one who can see what's actually going on. 

I mean, think about it. If I had a stroke or a brain injury, wouldn't I be slurring my words? Wouldn't I forget things? But I remember everything. I remember every single dollar I had, every single excuse they gave me, every single time they brought out those fake bank papers. My memory is sharp as a tack. I can tell you exactly what they said to me last Tuesday when I asked about the fundraiser money. So no, there's no brain illness, no head injury, nothing like that. I'm just a normal, healthy person who is being robbed blind by her own family, and they're using this whole "she's sick" routine to get away with it.

turns.doctor_question: Did these beliefs start or get much worse after you began using any alcohol, drugs, or new medications?
turns.patient_response:
No. No, definitely not. I mean, I don't even drink. Maybe a glass of wine at a wedding or something, but I don't keep alcohol in the house, I don't go to bars, none of that. And drugs? Please. I've never touched a drug in my life. I don't even like taking Tylenol unless I absolutely have a splitting headache, which I rarely do anyway. And as for new medications, no, I don't take anything. Like I said before, I'm healthy. I don't have any prescriptions, I don't take any pills. 

They would love it if I was on drugs, wouldn't they? That would be the perfect excuse! "Oh, don't listen to her, she's on drugs, she's drunk, it's the medication talking." But they can't use that one on me because I am completely clean. I am completely sober. My mind is clear. 

I know they probably told you I was on something, or maybe they're hoping you'll prescribe me something so I *will* be on something and then my mind will get all cloudy and I'll forget about the money. Is that why you're asking? Are you trying to find a reason to give me pills? Because I won't take them. I don't need them. I'm not taking anything now, and I wasn't taking anything when I first figured out what they were doing with my bank accounts. 

I remember the exact day it all clicked for me. I was completely sober, hadn't even had a cup of coffee yet. It was a Tuesday, early morning, and I was looking at a bank statement they had left out on the kitchen counter—probably by accident, or maybe they were testing me to see if I'd notice the discrepancies. And I did notice. I noticed right away. No drugs, no alcohol, no new medications. Just me, wide awake, seeing the truth right there on the paper, seeing how the numbers didn't add up to what they should have been. So no, nothing like that caused this. This isn't a side effect of anything. It's just the truth.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses clear persecutory delusions, believing that 'they' are stealing money from her bank accounts, trying to discredit her by claiming she is on drugs, and hoping the doctor will prescribe medication to cloud her mind so she forgets about the stolen money.

turns.doctor_question: Do you ever feel like other people can hear your thoughts, read your mind, or control what you think?
turns.patient_response:
Read my mind? No, no, I don't... I mean, that's impossible, right? People can't just reach into your head and hear what you're thinking. That's sci-fi stuff, like in those movies my brother used to watch when we were kids. Nobody can hear my thoughts. They wouldn't need to anyway, because I tell them exactly what I think to their faces! I tell them, "I know what you're doing, I know you're taking my money," so they don't have to guess what's in my head. 

And control my thoughts? No, nobody controls my thoughts but me. I'm the one connecting the dots. I'm the one who sits in my room and goes over the bank statements and remembers how much was supposed to be in there from the church fundraiser and how much is actually there now. That's all me. My brain is doing the work. If they could control my thoughts, they would have made me forget all about the money by now, wouldn't they? They would have just pushed a button in my head and made me think everything was fine and dandy. But they can't. Because my mind is my own. 

It just really gets under my skin that you're asking me these kinds of things. It's like you're trying to check off boxes on some kind of "crazy person" list. "Does she hear voices? Check. Does she think people are reading her mind? Check." Well, you can't check that box for me, doctor. I know they can't read my mind. I know they can't control me. What they *can* do is lie, and cheat, and forge documents, and whisper behind my back, and try to convince you that I'm the one with the problem. But they can't get inside my head. My thoughts are perfectly safe, and they are perfectly clear. I know exactly what's real and what isn't.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any problems with your memory or thinking lately?

No, absolutely not. My memory is perfect. I mean, I just told you, didn't I? I remember exactly what happened last Tuesday, I remember the exact day I figured out what they were doing with the bank statements. I can remember conversations word for word. Like, just the other day, my sister was standing in the hallway, right by the thermostat—she always messes with the thermostat, by the way, turns it down so it's freezing—and she said, "Oh, we don't know where that receipt went." I remember the exact tone of her voice, that fake innocent tone she uses when she thinks she's pulling one over on me. 

My thinking is completely sharp. It has to be, right? If my thinking was messed up, I wouldn't have been able to put all the pieces together. I wouldn't have noticed that the deposits from the church fundraiser didn't match the withdrawals they were making for "household expenses." Who spends four hundred dollars on groceries in three days? Nobody, that's who. I did the math. I sat down at the kitchen table with a calculator and a notepad, and I went through every single line item. Does that sound like someone who has problems with their thinking? 

It's actually really insulting that you would even ask that. It's like you're trying to find a loophole. "Oh, she doesn't have a brain injury, she's not on drugs, so maybe she's just getting forgetful or confused." But I'm not confused! I'm the only one who *isn't* confused! They want you to think I'm confused because it's easier to dismiss someone if you just say, "Oh, her memory is going, she doesn't know what she's talking about." But I know exactly what I'm talking about. I haven't forgotten a single thing they've done to me. Every lie, every missing dollar, every fake excuse—it's all filed away right here in my head. So no, my memory and my thinking are just fine. Better than fine, actually. They're exactly what's keeping me from letting them get away with this.

turns.doctor_question: About how long have you been convinced that your family is taking or hiding your money?
turns.patient_response:
Well, if you want to know exactly when I figured it all out, you have to understand the timeline of everything. It wasn't just some random day where I woke up and decided to be suspicious. There was a very specific trigger, a very specific moment when things started to shift. 

It was about a year and two months ago. I know that for a fact because that was right around the time my income dropped. I had some changes in my financial situation, you know, money wasn't coming in the way it used to. And you'd think your family would be supportive during a time like that, right? You'd think they'd rally around you and say, "Oh, don't worry, we'll tighten our belts, we'll figure it out together." But no, that's not what happened at all. 

Instead, the moment my income dropped—literally the exact same month, about fourteen months ago—that's when the weirdness started. That's when I started noticing the little things. A receipt missing here, a weird charge on the statement there. At first, I thought, okay, maybe things are just tight and they're stressed, maybe they're just bad at budgeting. But then I started really looking. I started tracking every penny. And I realized it wasn't just bad budgeting. It was deliberate. 

So, yes, it's been going on for a year and two months. Fourteen long months of me having to watch my back, having to double-check every piece of mail, every bank statement, every grocery receipt they bring into this house. Fourteen months of them thinking I'm stupid enough to just let it happen because I don't have as much money coming in as I used to. They probably thought, "Oh, she's stressed about her income dropping, she won't even notice if we skim a little off the top, she'll just blame it on her financial situation." 

But they underestimated me. They completely underestimated how closely I pay attention. I mean, a year and two months is a long time to keep up a lie, and they're getting sloppy. But I'm not. I've been onto them since the very beginning, since the day my income changed. I haven't let my guard down for a single second in all these months, and I'm not going to start now.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a fixed, persecutory belief that their family is deliberately stealing their money and lying to them, a conviction they have held firmly for 14 months.

turns.doctor_question: Do you have any other unusual fixed beliefs besides the money being hidden or stolen?
turns.patient_response:
Unusual fixed beliefs? Listen to yourself, doctor. You make it sound like I believe in aliens or ghosts or something. It's not a "belief," and it's definitely not unusual to want your own money to stay where it belongs. It's just the truth. 

The only reason I'm even sitting in this chair right now, the only reason I came in here today, is because my family and my friends—people who are supposed to have my back, mind you—they keep waving these bank papers in my face. They print out these little summaries and they point at the numbers and they say, "Look, look, the math adds up, the bank papers prove nothing was taken!" Like I'm stupid or something. Like I can't see right through what they're doing. 

I don't have any other "beliefs" because I'm too busy dealing with this one massive reality. For over a year now, I've known they're hiding my money. I've known it, and I've watched them do it. They're getting really crafty about how they do it, too. They think they can just shuffle things around and I won't notice the patterns. They use the regular household bills, right? They inflate the electric bill, or they say the water bill was extra high this month, and they funnel it out that way. And then there's the church fundraisers I mentioned before—they use those to siphon it off, pretending it's a donation. And don't even get me started on these sudden trip plans. Oh yeah, my sister is suddenly talking about planning this big weekend getaway, and I'm sitting there thinking, "With whose money? Where is that money coming from all of a sudden?" 

They use all of it—the bills, the fundraisers, the fake trip plans—just to cover up the fact that they are taking what's mine. They think if they create enough paperwork, I'll just get confused and give up. But I won't. I have to keep confronting them. I have to wake up every single day and get right in their faces about the receipts and the deposits, and I will keep doing it. I will keep pushing and asking questions and demanding answers until they finally crack and tell the truth. They want me to just shut up and accept their little bank papers, but I won't let them get away with it.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient describes a fixed, unyielding belief that their family and friends are stealing and hiding their money, despite contradictory evidence like bank statements, which is a clear persecutory delusion.

turns.doctor_question: In the past year, have you had a time when you felt very depressed or lost interest in things for at least two weeks?
turns.patient_response:
Depressed? No. I mean, who has the time to just sit around and be depressed for two whole weeks? Not me, that's for sure. If I just gave up and lost interest in things, like you're saying, they would have completely cleaned me out by now. You think I can just pull the covers over my head and cry? No way. I have to be on top of everything, every single day.

It makes me really, really angry when my own sister looks me in the eye and lies about a grocery run, or when they act like I'm the crazy one for asking to see the actual paper water bill instead of just taking their word for it. It's frustrating, you know? It gets my blood boiling. I get stressed out because I'm the only one in that house who actually cares about the truth. But angry isn't depressed. Depressed means you don't care anymore, right? Like you just want to sleep and you lose interest in what's going on around you. 

Well, my interest is at an all-time high. I am a hundred percent interested in where every single dime of my money is going. I don't have the luxury of losing interest. I'm up by six every morning, making my coffee, and I get straight to work. I check the online banking, I go out to the mailbox before anyone else is even awake, I even go through the recycling bin on the side of the house to see if they tried to throw away any receipts from the hardware store or the gas station. If I was depressed, I wouldn't be doing all that. I wouldn't have the energy. I'd just be letting them win and letting them take whatever they want. So no, I haven't been depressed at all. I'm just busy. I'm way too busy watching my back to be sad.

turns.patient_response:
Me? In a mental hospital? No. No, absolutely not. I've never had any of those things... what did you call it, schizophrenia? Bipolar? No, never. I've never been in any kind of psychiatric hospital, not once in my entire twenty-eight years on this earth. My brain works just fine. 

Honestly, I bet that’s exactly what they want you to think, though. My family, I mean. I bet they would just love it if you diagnosed me with one of those things you just said. They’d probably throw a party. Because think about it, doctor—if you write down on your little notepad there that I’m crazy, that I have some sort of mental problem, then they’re off the hook, aren't they? It’s the perfect excuse. They can just point at me and say, "Oh, don't listen to her, she's got bipolar, she belongs in a hospital," and then nobody will ever look into all the money they've been siphoning out of my accounts. They want to discredit me so they can keep getting away with it. 

But before this whole nightmare started fourteen months ago, nobody ever said a single word about my mental health. Nobody. I was just a normal person going about my business. Nobody ever looked at me and said I needed a psychiatrist or pills or a hospital. Not until I started asking the hard questions. Not until I started demanding to see the actual utility bills and the bank statements. It’s funny how that works, isn't it? The second you start catching people in their lies, the second you don't let them just walk all over you, suddenly they want to lock you up and call you crazy. But I have a completely clean record. No mental health problems, ever. And they know that. They're just grasping at straws because they know I'm onto them and I'm not backing down.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any trouble keeping up with your daily activities, work, or relationships since this started?
turns.patient_response:
Trouble? No. No, I don't have any trouble keeping up with my day-to-day stuff. I mean, yeah, obviously the relationships part is... well, it's strained. We argue. We argue all the time, pretty much every day. But that’s just about the money! Other than the arguments about them stealing from me, everything else is exactly the same as it’s always been. 

I still handle all my own meals, for one thing. I get up, I make my breakfast, I fix my own lunch, I don't expect anyone to cook for me or do anything for me. And my personal space? I keep my things in order the exact same way I always have. My room is completely organized. I know where every single item I own is placed. I mean, I have to, right? Because if I don't keep my things in perfect order, how am I going to know if they’ve been in there digging through my stuff while I’m in the bathroom? So I keep everything tight. I fold my clothes the same way, I keep my personal papers stacked up exactly where I left them. Everything is where it belongs. 

And I get out of the house just fine, too. I still get myself down to the county clinic whenever I need to go. I walk down to the stop, I take the bus, I get there early, I sign in. I don't need anyone holding my hand. Same thing with my assistance appointments. I never, ever miss an assistance appointment. I make sure I have my folder, I sit in the waiting room, I talk to the people I need to talk to... I do everything I'm supposed to do. I have to stay on top of all that, you know? I have to make sure my assistance paperwork is completely by the book so the county knows I'm responsible, especially with my family trying to pull the wool over everyone's eyes and mess with my accounts. 

So no, I'm not falling behind on anything. I'm handling my life perfectly fine. I don't have a job to go to, but my job right now is keeping track of what's mine, and I work very hard at it. The only trouble I have is the people I live with trying to rob me blind, and me having to fight them on it. But my actual daily routine? I'm doing exactly what I've always done.

Energized? Like, bouncing off the walls or something? No, definitely not. And I definitely don't need less sleep. I need my sleep, I really do. turns.doctor_question: Do you believe any strange or impossible things are happening, like someone controlling your body or people putting thoughts into your mind?
turns.patient_response:
What? Controlling my body? Putting thoughts in my mind? No. No, of course not. I mean, how would somebody even do that? It just... it honestly offends me a little bit that you would even ask me something like that. It really does. Because it sounds like you're trying to make me out to be some kind of lunatic who believes in magic or mind-readers or ghosts or something. I'm talking about real, actual things here. Real dollars and cents being stolen from me. Not mind control. I don't even know where you'd get an idea like that, unless... wait, did they tell you to ask me that? Did my family tell you I was talking about mind control to try and make me look bad? Because if they did, that's just another massive lie on top of the pile. They know I don't believe in any of that nonsense. My mind is perfectly fine, it belongs completely to me, and nobody is putting anything in it.

turns.patient_response:
Special devices? Like hidden cameras and wires? No, no, they don't need anything fancy like that. They aren't secret agents, they aren't using high-tech computers or whatever. They're doing it right out in the open, using regular everyday things, which is honestly almost worse if you think about it. 

Actually, that's exactly why I came in here, because my family and my friends—well, people I used to think were my friends—they all keep ganging up on me. They keep saying that the bank papers prove nothing was taken. They literally print out these statements, shove them right in my face, and go, "Look, look at the math, the numbers are right here, nothing is missing!" But they're lying. They are completely lying to my face and they expect me to just swallow it. 

For over a year now, well over a whole entire year, I’ve known for an absolute fact that they’re hiding my money. I know it in my bones. And they don't need hidden wires to do it, they just use normal stuff to cover it up. Like bills, for instance. They'll tell me the electric bill was extra high this month, or the groceries cost more, and they use that as a convenient little excuse for where the cash went. Or fundraisers! My sister was going on and on about this big fundraiser she was doing for some community thing, acting like she's some saint donating all this cash. I know exactly whose cash she was donating. It was mine! 

And then they have all these trip plans. They're always talking about going out of town for the weekend or taking a vacation, and they think I'm too stupid to notice that they're using my money to pay for their little getaways. They don't have that kind of extra income! They just shuffle the numbers around on those bank papers to make it look like legitimate expenses, or like I spent it myself. It's a massive cover-up, and they are all in on it together. 

It makes me so incredibly mad because they think I'm just going to back down just because they waved a piece of paper at me. But I'm not backing down. I'm really, really not. I have to keep confronting them about it. I bring it up at breakfast, I bring it up when they get home, I point out the fake bills and the trips they shouldn't be able to afford. I don't care if it causes a huge screaming match in the middle of the kitchen. I don't care if they roll their eyes at me. I am going to keep confronting every single one of them until they finally crack and tell the truth. They can't keep this lie going forever, they just can't. Eventually, someone is going to slip up and admit exactly what they did with my money, and I am not going to stop pushing them until that happens.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever had any episodes like this earlier in adulthood, before the past year?
turns.patient_response:
Earlier in adulthood? Like when I was eighteen or twenty or something? No. Absolutely not. Nothing like this ever happened back then. I mean, back then, things were fine. I trusted them, they trusted me, nobody was sneaking around or lying about the bills or trying to trick me. We actually got along okay for the most part. So no, this is not some lifelong thing that just happens to me. I am not crazy, like I keep trying to tell you. There is a very specific reason why this is happening right now, and a very specific time it all started. 

This whole entire situation, this whole nightmare with them taking my money and covering it up, it has been going on since my income dropped. That was about a year and two months ago. I know the exact timeline because I keep track of absolutely everything. I have to. See, about fourteen months ago, my income went down. I lost some of the money I had coming in regularly, and things got a lot tighter for me financially. And you would think your own flesh and blood would help you out when something like that happens, right? You would think they would be supportive and help you figure out a new budget. But no. The second my income dropped, that is exactly when they started siphoning off what little I had left. 

It is like they thought I would not notice because I was stressed out about having less money, or maybe they thought they could just take advantage of the confusion when my budget changed. But I noticed right away. I remember sitting at the kitchen table, looking at the numbers from that very first month after my income went down, a year and two months ago, and I thought to myself, wait a minute, this math does not add up. And it has not added up a single day since then. Every single month, it is the exact same story. So no, this is not some made-up thing from years and years ago. It started exactly fourteen months ago, right when my income dropped and they saw an opportunity to kick me when I was already down. I have the papers to prove the exact month it started, even if they keep trying to say those same papers prove something else.

turns.doctor_question: Before this started, had you ever had any recent changes in your thinking, behavior, or personality that others noticed?
turns.patient_response:
Changes in my thinking? Or my personality? No. No, not at all. I am the exact same person I have always been. I mean, my brain works perfectly fine, I think exactly the same way I always have. If anything, I’m probably thinking clearer now because I have to be so focused on everything they’re doing. But before this started? No, absolutely no changes. I was just living my life, doing my normal everyday things, acting like I always act. 

If anyone—and I mean anyone, like my sister or my old friends or whoever—tries to come in here and tell you that I was acting weird or my personality changed right before all this money stuff started, they are flat out lying to you. They are just trying to set up a story, you know? They want to make it look like, "Oh, look at her, she’s acting so different, she’s not herself," so that when I finally caught them stealing, they could just blame it on me and say my brain wasn't working right! But it’s a trick. It’s a total trick to make me look bad. 

I have always been me. I didn’t just wake up one day and get a whole new personality. I've always been observant, I've always been someone who pays attention to what's going on around the house. I mean, sure, maybe my behavior is a little different *now* because I'm angry, but who wouldn't be? If your own family was taking your cash and waving fake bank papers in your face, your behavior would change too! You'd start yelling in the kitchen too! You have to defend yourself. But before that? Before my income dropped fourteen months ago and they started their little scheme? No. I was perfectly normal. Nothing changed with my thinking, nothing changed with how I act. 

So if they told you I was acting different back then, you can just go ahead and cross that right out of your notes. It is just another one of their excuses to cover their tracks, because they know I'm onto them and they are getting desperate. But my mind is sharp. I know exactly who I am.

turns.doctor_question: Have these beliefs made it harder for you to do your usual work, take care of yourself, or get along with other people?
turns.patient_response:
Harder to take care of myself? No, absolutely not. I mean, obviously, like I just said, there are the arguments. So yeah, getting along with people is hard right now, but only because I have to fight them tooth and nail over my own cash! Other than the arguments about the money, which they cause by lying to my face, I am completely fine. I am functioning perfectly. 

I still handle my own meals every single day. I go into the kitchen, I make my own food, I clean up my own dishes—I actually prefer doing it myself now because I don't want them anywhere near my stuff, and who knows what they'd try to charge me for groceries if I let them cook for me. So I make my breakfast, I make my lunch, I do all of that completely on my own. 

And I still get to all my appointments, too. I never miss a single one. I get myself down to the county clinic whenever I need to, and I make sure I go to all my assistance appointments. I have to stay on top of that stuff, especially with my income being lower now and them stealing from me, so I make absolutely sure I am always there. I get myself there, on time, sitting in the chair waiting for my name to be called, filling out whatever forms they need. I don't need anyone holding my hand to get to the assistance office or the clinic. 

And my things? My belongings? I keep my things in order the exact same way I always have. My room is clean, my clothes are put away, my important papers are organized in neat little stacks so I know exactly where everything is. I have a whole system for my paperwork now so they can't shuffle things around without me noticing. So no, knowing what they are doing hasn't stopped me from taking care of myself. I handle my meals, my county clinic visits, my assistance appointments, and my chores just like I always did. They're the ones ruining everything with their lies, not me.

turns.doctor_question: Have you become more socially withdrawn or started avoiding other people more than before, apart from the arguments about your money?
turns.patient_response:
Me? Avoiding people? No, no, you have it completely backwards, doctor. I am not the one hiding in my room. I'm not avoiding anybody. It is them. They are the ones avoiding me! And it is so incredibly obvious what they are doing. 

Like with my bills, for example. I used to have my relatives come over and help me sort through the utility bills and the rent statements, just to make sure everything was paid up and the math was right. Sometimes the forms are confusing, and they used to sit right there at the kitchen table with me and help me figure out what I owed. But now? The second I bring up the missing money—which I have to bring up, because it is my money and it is missing!—they suddenly have somewhere else to be. And we used to plan trips! We were talking about taking a bus down to the coast, a whole travel plan for the summer, just a fun getaway with the girls. We had brochures and everything. But now? Nothing. Absolute crickets. They have completely stopped including me in the fundraisers. They stopped inviting me on the travel plans. I hear them talking about the trips, and my name isn't even mentioned anymore. 

And why do you think that is? Because I keep bringing up the money! That is the only reason! I try to warn them, I try to tell them, "Hey, you need to watch your wallets, because look what my own family is doing to me," and instead of thanking me for looking out for them, they just cut me out. They don't want to hear about the money. They don't want to deal with the fact that I am standing up for myself and demanding answers. It makes them uncomfortable because they probably don't want to believe that people can be so sneaky. So no, I am not withdrawing from anyone. I am perfectly happy to go to a fundraiser or go on a trip or sit down and do my bills, but they are the ones shutting me out and avoiding me just because I refuse to stay quiet about my own cash!
